newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - March 20.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's Daily Variety:

* Rysher Entertainment plans to slow its rate of feature film production to between three and five films in the coming year. It would now focus mostly on films with budgets below $15 million, Rysher CEO Keith Samples said.
* Robert Redford's Sundance Institute is considering putting on its name on the marquee of an arthouse circuit, industry sources said.

* Studio executives are watching the high level of inhouse production, especially at News Corp's Fox and General Electric's NBC. News Corp Chairman Rupert Murdoch has made no secret he wants the company to own as much product as possible.
* NBC affiliates are preparing for a showdown with Peacock web CEO Bob Wright about the issue of reusing the web's programming on cable outlets.
* Bruckheimer Films, looking to boost its presence in television, has hired Fox programming executive Jonathan Littman as senior vice president to oversee TV programming.
* Viacom's Paramount Domestic TV renewed its top magazine franchise Entertainment Tonight on eight stations owned by Westinghouse's CBS through the year 2000.
